description: Use this when a user asks what childcare costs parents: the price of a nursery, daycare, childminder or after-school place for a baby, toddler, preschool or school-age child in a county, region, state or city, or how childcare prices compare, in England (country GB), Ireland (country IE), Norway (country NO) or the United States (country US). These are official surveys and statistics of the fees providers charge parents (or what households report paying), not adverts or listings, and they are before public subsidies or funded hours unless the answer says otherwise. Each answer is an official average or median (price_type official_statistic): the range fields are null, and there is a sample size only where the publisher gives one. Every answer states its unit (for example US dollars per week, or pounds per hour), the year it describes, a confidence label, and the official source and licence. How fresh: England: calendar year 2025 (survey fieldwork May to July 2025, published 11 December 2025; next release December 2026); Ireland: 2016 only (CSO has not repeated the table); regional, not county; ten years old; Norway: annual (January figures); the 2026 figures were published on 30 April 2026; the United States: county prices for 2022 (the latest year the Department of Labor has published; the database lags by several years). Some of this data is several years old: always read the period in the answer. Do not use for the cost of a specific nursery, advertised fees or waiting-list prices, the value of government subsidies, tuition for schools or universities, babysitting or nanny wages, or other countries.

age_group.description: Age of the child: infant (under 2), toddler (2), preschool (3 to 4 or until school), school-age. Each source says how it defines them. Leave out for the source's default (see the answer). GB: infant (under 2), toddler (2), preschool (3 and 4; default) or school-age (regions only). IE: only 'pre-school' (infant, toddler and preschool all give the pre-school children figure) or school-age (primary school children); leave out for all children aged 0 to 12. NO: ignored; the table averages all kindergarten children. US: infant (under 2), toddler (2), preschool (3 years old to school age) or school-age. Default infant.

area.description: Place: a county, a region, a local authority, or a state or city where the source says so (examples: 'Cook County, IL', 'London', 'Dublin'). Leave out for the whole country, where the source has a national figure. GB: England (leave out), a region (London, North West ...) or a local authority (Manchester, Leeds, Camden ...). Local authorities are published for 2 year olds and 3 and 4 year olds only. IE: a county, city or region such as Dublin, Cork, Galway or Mid-West; the answer is for the CSO region it belongs to. Leave out for the whole State. NO: a municipality such as Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim, Stavanger or Tromso (Norwegian spellings work). Leave out for the whole country. US: required. A county, for example 'Cook County, IL' or 'Harris County, Texas' (add the state when the name is not unique). Cities, ZIP codes and states are not published; use the county.

care_type.description: centre = nursery, daycare or group-based setting; home-based (also childminder) = a registered provider caring in their own home. Leave out for centres or for all providers, as the source says. GB: centre (shown as private group-based providers) or home-based (childminders); England as a whole only. Leave out for all providers. IE: ignored; the table averages all paid childcare. NO: ignored; the table averages all kindergartens. US: centre (child care centre; default) or home-based (family childcare in the provider's home; also written childminder).

country.description: GB = England only (DfE provider survey; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are not covered); IE = Ireland (CSO survey of what households pay for childcare, 2016, by region); NO = Norway (Statistics Norway average kindergarten fees by municipality, January); US = United States (Department of Labor county childcare prices, 2022)

hours.description: Full-time or part-time care, where a source publishes both. Most sources publish one basis only and say which. GB: ignored; fees are per hour, with no full-time or part-time split. IE: ignored; the table averages part-time and full-time use. NO: ignored; the table gives one monthly average. US: full-time only (weekly prices); part-time is not published.

name: pricepaid_childcare_prices

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.

title: Childcare prices paid
